conflict_topics: cooking schedule / rotation and late slots
whose obligation to wash pans and when
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants offered concrete proposals and reasons (sleep/early shift, working from home) rather than abstract complaints.
C moved to operationalize decisions by creating a shared note and rota — practical step that advanced implementation.
There is minimal needless repetition; most turns add a new detail or acceptance.
evaluation.final_reason: Several substantive issues were agreed: use of extractor fan and closing corridor door and avoiding late cooking before B's early shift (A: "I won't cook late before your early shift, and I'll use the extractor fan and close the corridor door when I cook late."), the rule that whoever cooks washes their pan the same night, and a shared note to track supplies with monthly settlement (C: "we track shared supplies in a shared note and settle monthly"). The parties also began implementing a weekly rotation (C: "we keep Agent D's weekly early/late rotation..." and D was scheduled for the late slot that week). However, Agent A's specific demand to keep one late slot every other week remains unaddressed and thus unresolved (A: "I need to keep one late slot every other week since I work from home"). Because most issues were settled but this scheduling exception was not resolved, final_status is partially_resolved.
position_change_notes: Agent A: retained their request for an exception ("I need to keep one late slot every other week") but conceded to extractor use and avoiding late cooking before B's early shift.
Agent B: moved from complaint to practical offer—willing to take early slots and proposed concrete extractor/door measures and reimbursement options.
Agent C: shifted into coordinator role, proposing the rota, shared note, and monthly settlement and offering to implement them.
Agent D: proposed the initial rotation and accepted the operational plan, asking to be scheduled for the first late slot; no backtracking on the rotation was recorded.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 (Agent D): "two people cook earlier, two later, and we rotate the late slot each week. Also, whoever cooks washes their own pan." vs Turn 2 (Agent A): "can I keep some late slots sometimes?" — A accepts rotation but requests an exception to the proposed strict rotation.

Turn 3 (Agent B) requests constraints for late cooking: "avoid late cooking the night before my early shift... use the extractor fan and close the corridor door" and offers to take early slots. Turn 4 (Agent A) agrees to B's constraints but reiterates: "I need to keep one late slot every other week since I work from home." Several points are agreed, but A's exception to the rotation remains unresolved.

Turn 5 (Agent B) offers a supplies settlement: split / reimburse monthly or track receipts. Turn 6 (Agent C) proposes: "we keep Agent D's weekly early/late rotation, whoever cooks that night washes their pan, and we track shared supplies in a shared note and settle monthly." Many items are adopted, but C's rota statement does not address A's request for a preserved late slot, so that incompatibility persists.

Turn 7 (Agent D): "please make the shared note and put me down for a late slot this week so the rotation starts." and Turn 8 (Agent C): "I'll make the shared note now and put you down for the late slot this week." This moves from negotiation into scheduling that could conflict with A's stated need to retain a late slot every other week.

Turn 9 (Agent D): "No objections. Sounds good — please go ahead and put me down for the late slot this week." and Turn 10 (Agent C): "Okay — I'll create the shared note and put you down for this week's late slot." The group proceeds with the rotation schedule without resolving A's previously stated exception.

Turn 11 (Agent D): "Okay." No new concessions or adjustments are recorded; the rota is being started in a way that appears incompatible with Agent A's request to retain one late slot every other week (A's line in Turn 4: "I need to keep one late slot every other week since I work from home").

substantive_insights: Main tension is scheduling: a simple weekly rotation conflicts with Agent A's need for extra late slots due to working from home.
Smell management is actionable (extractor, corridor door) and was accepted, which reduces one source of friction.
Financial/household supply issue was resolved by agreeing to track supplies in a shared note and monthly settlement, removing a potential recurring source of dispute.
